findings.title: Checker's exit status is never tested
findings.description: The new script adds a direct-invocation check that reads `process.argv[2]` as the directory and sets `process.exitCode` to 1 when any problem is found. The only test in `tests/checkout-credentials.test.ts` calls `persistedCredentials` and `workflowCredentialProblems` as functions, so no case runs the script as a child process and checks its stdout or exit status. A regression in the entry block, the argument handling, or the exit code would pass `npm run check` unnoticed, and the diff does not add or update any case in `tests/cli.test.ts`.

citations.citation: Test CLI boundary changes through a real child process

evidence.explanation: The PR changes argument handling (`process.argv[2]`), exit codes (`process.exitCode = problems.length === 0 ? 0 : 1`) and the direct-invocation check (`path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`). The added tests import only the exported functions, so the rule's requirement for a child-process case is not met.

findings.title: A checkout step spelled in other letter case passes unchecked
findings.description: `persistedCredentials` returns early for case-variant checkout names because `MENTION` is case-sensitive, while `STEP` is also case-sensitive. A pinned `uses: Actions/Checkout@<sha>` step without `persist-credentials: false` still runs as checkout on GitHub, but this check skips it and the action-pin check accepts it.

citations.citation:
2. A test in `tests/` reads every `.github/workflows/*.yml` file and fails, naming the file and
   the line, when a checkout step does not set `persist-credentials: false`. It fails closed:
   a line that mentions `actions/checkout` in any other form than a block `uses:` step, a step
   whose next line is not its own `with:`, an option given twice, a value other than `false`,
   or a flow mapping is reported, not passed. It runs in `npm run check`.

evidence.explanation: At line 54, `persistedCredentials` returns unless `MENTION` or `QUOTED_USES` matches; neither regex is case-insensitive, and an unquoted line without a backslash does not match `QUOTED_USES`. The independent action-pin check permits uppercase owner and repository characters, so a pinned case-variant checkout line produces no credential problem and is not rejected by the pin check.

findings.title: Ticket-link check stays red on this PR
findings.description: The new T-035 BACKLOG row reads `planned`, but the ticket-link check requires `done (PR <n>)` for any ticket named in the title or closed by the PR, so that check fails at this head. The author notes say this is red by design until a second commit sets the row to `done (PR n)`, so the required green ticket-link run is absent on this pull request.

Please refresh the Day 16 gate record before using it for a merge decision; it still reflects the pre-review state despite later review results being committed alongside it.

The credential check currently covers workflows directly under `.github/workflows`, which includes all current checkouts, but it would not cover checkout steps in future composite actions under `.github/actions/`. Consider documenting that scope in `AGENTS.md`.

Before relying on the agent lane again, please run both the labelled-ticket and `@claude`-comment paths, as criterion 6 calls for. The available evidence that the action re-authenticates before its git operations comes only from the `v1`-tag log.
